question: Tell me about a time you strongly disagreed with a teammate or your manager on a technical decision.
followUps: What exactly was each side's position and why?
How did you communicate your view — what did you actually say or write?
How was it resolved, and would you handle it the same way again?
How is your relationship with that person now?
strongSignals: Disagrees with data, not ego; seeks to understand the other view
Escalates only after trying to resolve directly
Commits fully once a decision is made (disagree and commit)
redFlags: Blames or belittles the other person
'We' everywhere with no personal actions
Story where they were simply right and nothing was learned

question: Tell me about a project or decision that failed or went badly. What was your role in it?
followUps: What specifically did you do that contributed to the failure?
When did you realise it was going wrong, and what did you do then?
What did you change in how you work afterwards?
Has that lesson helped you since? Give an example.
strongSignals: Owns their part clearly without deflecting
Concrete, lasting change in behaviour
Proportionate — neither trivial nor catastrophising
redFlags: A 'failure' that is really a disguised strength
Blames others or circumstances only
No concrete lesson or change

question: Tell me about a time you took ownership of a problem that wasn't strictly your responsibility.
followUps: Why did you decide to take it on?
What did you have to deprioritise to do it?
What obstacles did you hit and how did you get past them?
What was the measurable result?
strongSignals: Acts without being asked when it matters to the customer/team
Follows through to completion, not just raising the issue
Balances it against their own commitments
redFlags: Complains about others not doing their job
Starts but hands off halfway
No clear outcome

question: Describe a situation where you had to make progress on a project with unclear requirements or goals.
followUps: What did you do first to reduce the ambiguity?
Who did you talk to, and what did you learn?
What assumptions did you make and how did you validate them?
How did the result compare with what was eventually needed?
strongSignals: Breaks the problem down and gets early feedback
States assumptions explicitly and revisits them
Makes reversible decisions quickly
redFlags: Waits for someone to hand over perfect requirements
Builds a lot before checking direction

question: Tell me about a time you had to deliver something important under a very tight deadline.
followUps: What did you cut or simplify, and how did you decide?
How did you communicate risk to stakeholders?
What trade-offs did you make on quality, and how did you handle them later?
What would you do differently?
strongSignals: Prioritises ruthlessly and explains trade-offs
Communicates early about risk
Pays down shortcuts afterwards
redFlags: Heroics with no planning (worked 20 hours a day as the only answer)
Hid problems until the deadline

question: Tell me about a time you convinced people who didn't report to you to adopt your idea or change direction.
followUps: Who were the stakeholders and what did each care about?
What evidence or prototype did you use?
What pushback did you get and how did you address it?
What was the outcome?
strongSignals: Tailors the argument to each audience's goals
Uses data, prototypes or small experiments
Builds allies rather than forcing a decision
redFlags: Escalated to a manager as the first move
Idea adopted with no understanding of why

question: Tell me about a time you helped a teammate grow or become more effective.
followUps: What did you notice they needed?
What specifically did you do, week to week?
How did you know it was working?
What did you learn about mentoring from it?
strongSignals: Specific, sustained actions (pairing, reviews, stretch tasks)
Lets the person own the work
Observable improvement
redFlags: Just 'answered their questions'
Took over the work instead of teaching

question: Tell me about a time you went out of your way to solve a problem for a customer or user.
followUps: How did you find out about the problem?
How did you verify what the customer actually needed?
What trade-offs did you make for them?
How did you measure the impact?
strongSignals: Starts from the customer and works backwards
Distinguishes what they asked for from what they need
Uses metrics or feedback to confirm impact
redFlags: Customer only mentioned in passing
Built what was asked without questioning it

question: Walk me through the most significant technical decision you made in the last year.
followUps: What options did you consider and why did you reject them?
How did you evaluate risk and cost?
Who did you involve in the decision?
Looking back, was it the right call?
strongSignals: Clear options with explicit trade-offs
Considers long-term maintenance, not just speed
Honest retrospective
redFlags: Picked a technology because it was new/cool
No alternatives considered

question: Tell me about a time you had more work than you could possibly do. How did you decide what to do and what to drop?
followUps: What framework or criteria did you use?
How did you communicate what would not get done?
Did anyone disagree with your priorities? What happened?
What was the impact of the things you dropped?
strongSignals: Prioritises by impact and urgency with stakeholder input
Says no explicitly and transparently
Revisits priorities as things change
redFlags: Tried to do everything and burned out
Dropped things silently

question: Tell me about the toughest piece of feedback you've received. How did you respond?
followUps: How did you feel when you first heard it?
What did you do in the following weeks?
How did you check whether you had improved?
Have you given similar feedback to someone else?
strongSignals: Listens without defensiveness
Concrete action plan and follow-up
Seeks feedback proactively afterwards
redFlags: Dismisses the feedback as unfair
Trivial feedback chosen to look good

question: Tell me about a time you improved the quality, reliability or performance of a system or process your team owned.
followUps: How did you identify the problem — what signals or metrics?
What did you change and why that approach?
How did you get the team to adopt it?
What were the before and after numbers?
strongSignals: Uses metrics to find and prove the improvement
Fixes root causes, not symptoms
Makes the improvement stick (automation, standards)
redFlags: Vague 'made it better' with no data
One-off fix with no lasting change
